blockers.title: The mandatory retained trustDecision has no lawful retention location, and the one place it is named contradicts two extras-closed serializations
evidence: The v19 blocker required the successor to 'require and retain the exact successful signature/package trust decision ... and bind that result to the same resolved object or running-kernel subject.' v20 supplies the requirement four times: authenticityCore.trustDecisionRequired ('incomplete without a retained successful trustDecision'), both supportedPairs entries defining a closed extras-rejected trustDecision object, and fileBackedBinding ('MUST run the same pair for this profile and bind trustDecision plus authenticityCore to this event's resolvedObjectIdentity').

The subject contains exactly one statement of where that record lives: evidenceJoin.PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED, 'laterEventVariant.observedAttestation is PLATFORM-ATTESTED.authenticityCore plus the retained trustDecision from platformAttestationOperation.' A full traversal of the subject for the token trustDecision returns no other placement rule.

That single placement is contradicted by three live rules. authenticityCore.form is '{scheme, payload}. extrasRejected.' observedForm is 'exactly authenticityCore. No second schema.' loaderTraces.identitySerializations.observedAttestation is 'ALIAS. Not a second schema', producersEmit 'that canonical object only', extrasRejected true. An observedAttestation carrying a third member is therefore rejected by its own serialization rule.

The signed-entry side repeats the closure independently. volumeConstraint.tags.PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED.laterEventVariant.observedAttestation is 'required; PLATFORM-ATTESTED.authenticityCore / observedForm; not a second schema', the tag object lists no trustDecision member, and volumeConstraint.form states 'Extra fields rejected.' So the join rule and the signed tagged union disagree about the shape of the same later-event object.

sameSerialization compounds it: 'signed authenticityCore MUST equal observed authenticityCore field-for-field.' The signed envelope is closed to exactly {authenticityCore, optional sonameAbi} and carries no trustDecision, so an observed side that carries one cannot satisfy field-for-field equality.

For file-backed PLATFORM-ATTESTED events there is no placement at all. classMap makes loader and framework PLATFORM-ATTESTED-only and libc PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND, and pathlessClasses.members is only OS ABI, so loader, framework, and libc are mandatory non-pathless PLATFORM-ATTESTED classes. Their join variants are INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME and EXTERNAL-ORIGIN, and neither mentions trustDecision. fileBackedBinding demands the binding with no record to bind.

retainedEventSchema, the roster of retained later-event fields, has twenty entries and no trustDecision or platform-attestation-result field. The artifact's own discipline treats that roster as the required home for a mandatory retained observation: honestyRepairsFromV8 records 'companionObservation is a retainedEventSchema field with companionObservationShape' as the fix for exactly this defect class, and reviewGuidance.forTheIndependentReviewer nominates 'a companionObservation that is still unnamed in retainedEventSchema' as an attack the reviewer should run.

The result is not a naming quibble. Either the trustDecision is emitted, in which case observedAttestation and the PATHLESS laterEventVariant reject it and sameSerialization fails, or it is omitted, in which case trustDecisionRequired makes the observed core incomplete. Both branches refuse for every PLATFORM-ATTESTED event under a straight reading, while a producer following only the evidenceJoin sentence and ignoring the extras closures accepts. Two conforming implementations reach opposite outcomes on the same trace.
blockers.impact: OS ABI, loader, and framework are mandatory PLATFORM-ATTESTED classes and libc may be. The trust decision that v20 relies on to convert 'a returned identifier' into 'a platform attestation' is required but has no schema slot on the retained event, no slot on either observed serialization, and no slot at all on the non-pathless path where three of the four mandatory classes live. G22's testMatrix demands every complete platformProfile x every taxonomy class, so no reproducible security decision exists for those cells: implementations that honor the extras closures refuse universally, and implementations that honor the evidenceJoin sentence emit a record whose encoding, key names, and ordering this artifact never fixes. The v19 finding is restated rather than discharged.
blockers.requiredRepair: Name the retained trust decision as a first-class retained field. Add trustDecision to loaderTraces.retainedEventSchema with a closed shape of its own on loaderTraces.identitySerializations (interfaceId, status where the pair defines one, result, and the bound subject or resolvedObjectIdentity), stated as extrasRejected and as a sibling of observedAttestation rather than a member of it. Rewrite evidenceJoin.PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED so observedAttestation remains exactly authenticityCore and the trustDecision is joined alongside it, and add the same required trustDecision join to the INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME and EXTERNAL-ORIGIN variants and to the corresponding volumeConstraint laterEventVariant objects so loader, framework, and libc events carry it. Keep sameSerialization scoped to authenticityCore explicitly, exactly as it already scopes out sonameAbi.
blockers.confidence: CONFIRMED. Every quoted string was read from the pinned subject at digest f44e4023..., and the absence of any other trustDecision placement was established by exhaustive traversal of the parsed document, not by keyword sampling.

shouldFix.title: retainedEventSchema still triggers companionObservation off the payload location that the v19-S1 repair forbids for PLATFORM-ATTESTED
evidence: The v20 repair moves PLATFORM-ATTESTED sonameAbi out of the payload. companions.SONAME-ABI.encodingByTag reads 'signed-only envelope sibling sonameAbi ... beside authenticityCore. Never inside payload.' signedForm and optionalLibcCompanion agree, and authenticityCore.excludes states sonameAbi 'is never a member of authenticityCore'. companionObservationShape was updated in step: it triggers 'at the encodingByTag location: PLATFORM-ATTESTED envelope sibling, or DIGEST-BOUND libc payload field.'
retainedEventSchema item 18 was not updated. It still reads 'companionObservation (required on a libc event when the signed payload carries sonameAbi; absent otherwise)'.

For a PLATFORM-ATTESTED libc entry the signed payload can never carry sonameAbi, since that placement is now forbidden. The retained-schema rule therefore falls through to 'absent otherwise' and makes companionObservation mandatory-absent for exactly the case in which companionObservationShape.whenRequired says 'Observation is then mandatory, not best-effort' and companions.SONAME-ABI.comparison says 'the corresponding libc event MUST retain companionObservation.'

This is the same defect shape Codex raised as PTCB-V19-S1: the canonical rules were relocated while a live rule kept the old location, leaving no placement that satisfies both. v20 fixed the two rules Codex named and left a third one behind.

reviewGuidance.forTheIndependentReviewer nominates 'a companionObservation that is still unnamed in retainedEventSchema' as an attack. The field is named there, but named with a trigger condition that the repair made unsatisfiable for one of its two tags.
shouldFix.impact: Bounded, because sonameAbi is metadata only and presence, absence, or mismatch never changes allow or refuse. But a PLATFORM-ATTESTED libc entry carrying the optional companion has no single conforming retained record: one live rule requires companionObservation and another requires it absent, so two implementations produce different retained traces for the same signed input, and a trace-completeness check can read either as correct. The claimed PTCB-V19-S1 repair is therefore incomplete.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Restate retainedEventSchema item 18 in terms of the tag-relative location rather than the payload, for example: 'companionObservation (required on a libc event when a signed sonameAbi companion is present at companions.SONAME-ABI.encodingByTag for that entry's authenticity tag; absent otherwise)'. That wording tracks companionObservationShape.whenRequired and companions.SONAME-ABI.comparison for both PLATFORM-ATTESTED and DIGEST-BOUND without reintroducing the payload location.

advisories.title: Two knownIds publishers have no lawful package-db interface, so their profiles can never qualify
advisories.note: interfaceId is a closed enum of rpm-checksig | apt-secure selected by publisher, and api maps rpm-family publishers to the former and dpkg-family to the latter. knownIds includes alpine and arch, which are neither family. Those publishers are not OTHER-PUBLISHER, so the refuse clause reaches them only through 'an unnamed interface refuses'. The behavior is fail-closed and therefore sound, and unsupportedPairRefuses is honest that later successors add pairs. Recorded so a successor states the publisher-to-interface mapping explicitly, or moves alpine and arch out of knownIds, rather than leaving two enumerated publishers permanently unqualifiable by implication. Not scored: no unsound admit path, and coverage limits are already disclaimed.

advisories.title: packageBytes.collection is defined by reference to an unpinned external published rule
advisories.note: The definition is operation-relative rather than invented, digestInput excludes other files, signatures, and metadata unless the published rule includes them, and a rule that does not yield exactly one byte sequence refuses. That is a real advance on v19 and the ambiguous case is fail-closed. The residual is that 'the database's published membership/root rule' is not pinned to a named document or version, so this artifact alone cannot exclude two publishers reading it differently and each believing they obtained exactly one byte sequence. Since digest sits inside authenticityCore and participates in signed-to-observed equality, such a divergence surfaces as a refusal rather than a false allow. Recorded, not scored.

conclusion: REJECT. v20 makes real progress on PTCB-V19-B1: platformAttestationOperation names SecCodeCheckValidity and the rpm-checksig | apt-secure enum, forbids the bare cdhash query, requires signature-and-membership validity, binds the returned identifier to that same successful check, and gives packageBytes a fail-closed digest input. The v19 envelope hole is closed and the v19 resolver advisory is discharged. What survives is retention. The trustDecision that carries the entire repair is required in four places, is placed in exactly one, and that placement puts it inside observedAttestation, which is alias-locked to authenticityCore and extras-rejected on both the loaderTraces path and the signed volumeConstraint path, while sameSerialization demands field-for-field equality with a signed envelope that has no such member. On the non-pathless path where loader, framework, and libc live, there is no placement at all and no retainedEventSchema field, even though this contract's own v8 repair established that roster as the home for a mandatory retained observation. Separately, retainedEventSchema still gates companionObservation on the payload location that the v19-S1 repair forbade for PLATFORM-ATTESTED, leaving the same no-lawful-placement contradiction Codex found, one rule further down. 1 blocker, 1 SHOULD-FIX; ACCEPT requires zero of each. DR-126 remains OPEN and this artifact remains DO-NOT-SEAL.
